subject: Performance MAP + long-context validation plan for FinWare
messages:
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@finware.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP idea and perf variables

Marcus — thanks for the demo today. We liked the latency profile in the hosted demo, but before we sign a reserved capacity agreement we need a detailed MAP that captures how you will validate the long-context behavior and the expected production SLAs.

High level asks from my side:
- A clear test matrix for max context (we go up to 65k tokens in some ingestion flows)
- TTFT guarantees (time-to-first-token) for responses under 1s for short prompts and explained degradation for long prompts
- Concurrency: expected throughput at 8, 16, 64 concurrent streams
- KV cache behavior: cold vs warm cache expectations and how prefix caching affects amortized cost

Can you circulate a MAP and the evaluation plan by next week? Procurement will want the test artifacts for their security review.

Lisa
Lisa Gomez
Head of Product, FinWare
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@finware.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP + long-context validation plan for FinWare

Lisa — thanks, great notes. Attached is an initial MAP + evaluation plan (redwood_perf_plan_v3.pdf) and a compact perf matrix (perf_matrix_20250918.csv). High-level summary below and proposed MAP milestones.

Summary of our validation approach:
1) Scope & goals:
   - Validate latency (p50/p90/p99) and TTFT across prompt length spectrum (64 tokens -> 65k tokens).
   - Measure throughput (tokens/s) at concurrency points: 1, 8, 16, 32, 64.
   - Quantify KV cache delta: cold start vs warm KV cache and incremental prefix re-use.
   - Provide tuning guidance (batching, compilation knobs, quantization tradeoffs) to meet SLAs.

2) Test matrix (attached CSV):
   - Sequence lengths: 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768, 65536 (we will approximate 65k using chunking harness where model supports it).
   - Prompt distributions: (a) short-query (median 64), (b) mixed-prod (empirical trace from your staging logs — we'll sample 10k prompts), (c) long-doc (>=8k).
   - Concurrency runs: cold-run (no warmed KV), warm-run (KV cache prepopulated with 500 recent prefixes), load sweep across concurrency levels.

3) Measurement method:
   - Warmup: 200 requests per config; Measurement: 1000 requests (or until steady-state) per config.
   - TTFT: measured from request arrival to first token emitted at the client-facing interface (includes scheduling).
   - Throughput: tokens/s at steady state, measured at the gateway.
   - Server-side metrics: GPU utilization, memory (KV usage), kernel stalls.

4) Deliverables & MAP milestones:
   - 2025-09-15: Redwood runs initial matrix in our staging (synthetic). Deliver: perf matrix CSV, high-level notes.
   - 2025-09-18: Joint validation run with FinWare traces in your staging; deliver: joint report, recommendations.
   - 2025-09-22: Decision workshop + handoff runbook for production cutover and scaling knobs.

We propose a canary bound of 1% traffic initially, then 10% for 48 hours to validate stability once you sign.

Attachments: redwood_perf_plan_v3.pdf (plan), perf_matrix_20250918.csv (initial synthetic results).

I'll hold a short working session Monday 9/15 to walk through the matrix — can you confirm someone from SRE will be on the call?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: FinWare SRE <sre@finware.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@finware.com>, procurement@finware.com
Date: 2025-09-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP + long-context validation plan for FinWare

Marcus — quick notes after the joint run this morning. We ran the mixed-prod trace (10k samples) and the long-doc bucket (2k samples >= 8k tokens). Observations:

- TTFT (short-query median): 420ms (p50) in hosted demo; p90 ~ 780ms.
- Long-doc TTFT (first token for 16k prompts): median 1.6s, p90 3.8s when cold; warm-KV drops median to 920ms.
- Throughput: single-stream tokens/s drops substantially beyond 8k; at 32k context steady-state tokens/s is ~35% of 512-token baseline.
- Concurrency: at 32 concurrent streams we observed contention in the scheduler leading to 12% p99 latency increase; batching config adjustments recommended.

Questions for Redwood team:
1) How deterministic is the warm-KV effect across different model families (we saw variance between the v1.3 and v1.5 variants)?
2) Are there recommended batching targets for 32k and 65k contexts to avoid OOMs without increasing TTFT unacceptably?

We'll attach the raw logs; procurement wants the CVE/SOC artifacts but Lisa has those.

- FinWare SRE (Ben)
[attachment: finware_longcontext_trace_sample.json (JSON)]
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: FinWare SRE <sre@finware.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: 2025-09-16T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP + long-context validation plan for FinWare

Ben / team — thanks for the detailed notes. A few clarifications and actions based on the raw traces you shared: 

- Determinism of warm-KV: warm-KV benefit is consistent when the prefix reuse pattern is high; variance between model variants is expected because of differing kv-cache encoding and attention recompute. We will include model-variant specific baseline tables in the full report.
- Batching guidance for extreme contexts: for 32k+ contexts we recommend strict per-instance batching (batch size 1 or 2) with larger micro-batching at the I/O layer to avoid OOMs. Also using prefix compression + sharded KV storage reduces memory pressure.

Planned follow-ups (short timeline):
- 2025-09-17: We will run a model-variant dedicated sweep (v1.3, v1.5, q8_0 variants) on your mixed-prod trace and collect p50/p90/p99 + TTFT + tokens/s. Output will be appended to perf_matrix_20250918.csv and we will add an addendum kv_cache_impact_notes.txt.
- 2025-09-18: Joint results review + decision on reserved pool sizing (GPU count target) and canary schedule.

I've attached a short runbook snippet we can use for the cutover to reduce risk. Let me know if you want a deeper session on KV internals.

- Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: kv_cache_impact_notes.txt (txt)]
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@finware.com>, FinWare SRE <sre@finware.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, procurement@finware.com
Date: 2025-09-18T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP + long-context validation plan for FinWare

Team — we ran the variant sweep and attached the consolidated results (perf_matrix_20250918.csv updated). Key takeaways for the MAP decision:

- For your production distribution (trace-based sample) we can meet TTFT <=1s p50 for short queries consistently on the v1.5 quantized (q8_0) variant when warm-KV is active.
- For 32k+ documents, steady-state throughput falls, but warm-KV recovery and aggressive prefix caching recover ~40-60% of the throughput gap depending on prompt reuse.
- Concurrency sizing recommendation: for the initial reserved pool we recommend capacity sized to support 32 concurrent streams at target avg tokens/s observed in your trace (we provide the GPU count estimate in the attached CSV).

MAP next steps (agreed):
- 2025-09-19: Procurement to issue an order intent (procurement@finware.com).
- 2025-09-22: Production Cutover Workshop (decision & runbook).
- 2025-10-01: 30-day canary begins (1% -> 10% ramps per playbook).

I'll share the final MAP PDF with timelines once procurement confirms order intent. Thanks all for quick turnaround — good collaboration.

Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: final_map_short.pdf (PDF)]
